decisions.reason: The geometric map was not identified by matching differential formulas. Replaced the assertion that collapse homotopies restrict by two exactly commuting quotient squares: retained barred grids map into the larger grid, and retained bigons map into their named rows/columns. The actual good-cover inclusion now induces the retained cellular kernel inclusion; zero new coordinates prove saturation over the domain, including the zero smaller kernel at n=2.

F1 explicitly draws on the supplier proof constructions, not merely its single-arc Statement: steps 1.1–3.1 construct graph/face smoothing and steps 4.1–6.1 construct supported ambient reductions. Graph preservation is supplied separately by F2 and proved in the present steps 1.1–1.2. Consulted the complete Farb–Margalit Lemma 2.9 proof and Proposition 2.8: the two labelled chains are pairwise minimal/nonisotopic with no triple meeting, and the supported bigon/last-region moves preserve the arranged graph. Purity fixes endpoint labels and the increasing interval correction fixes the spine pointwise. The Joukowski completion gives a compact annulus with both shores fixed; its boundary-relative integer twist isotopy descends continuously. The n=1 case uses B1=1. The rejection incorrectly treats the supplier Statement as the only usable evidence and overlooks the separately cited graph argument.

F2 cites exact proof locators rather than attributing an unstated theorem to the dependency Statement. The current dependency actually constructs a graph containing an arc (1.1), a marked-relative smooth representative (2.1), finite transverse germs (3.1), compact terminal normalization and actual-cover projection (4.1–5.1), and supported ambient moves (6.1). The present item repeats the returning-track count and clean-bigon extraction for a disjoint crosscut family, including the shared-boundary-endpoint sector count. Least attainable finite count proves (i)–(ii); proper obstacles disjoint from both sides cannot lie within a puncture-free bigon, so support enlargement avoids them and proves (iii). AC and the proper-end convention are explicit. No unsupported strengthening or missing logical step is identified by this rejection.

The definition does not place the noncompact fork surface in the absolute first argument. Its existing forks/noodles dependency states the closed-replacement identity, and the cited well-definedness supplier proves exactly the needed extension in proof step 5.1: choose tine-puncture closing neighborhoods disjoint from the noodle, compare finite intersections of c_F=Delta_F times the fork outside those neighborhoods, obtain <c_F,y_N>=Delta_F times the labelled polynomial, and cancel the nonzero factor in the Laurent domain after finite prism comparisons. Its steps 1.1–4.1 prove finiteness, class independence and sesquilinearity for the absolute/end-stable pair. Thus the claimed independence is already proved by the cited item, including normalization, rather than an application of its Statement to two end-relative classes. The finite label loops return to opposite boundary endpoints and give the stated exponents and signs.

The original role swap compared the unproved maximality of m_{j,i}, so it did not establish b_{j,j}=b_{i,j}. Repaired step 5.1 keeps z_j-prime fixed and moves the unprimed point from z_j to z_i on the actual tine, returning from z_i to z_j on the noodle. Its labelled lift compares m_{i,j} directly with m_{j,j}; a positive detour supplies the +1 half-turn in the crossing case. Strict inequality gives positive winding. The cyclic-cover disk now counts a_{k,j}-a_{j,j}, which global q-maximality forces to zero, and its innermost projection gives a forbidden digon. Together with the existing first-coordinate argument, both diagonal t exponents agree and all maximal terms have the stated common sign. Read the full Bigelow Claim 3.4 argument; its final similar-comparison sentence was expanded here rather than assuming transpose maximality.

The cited well-definedness item proves the exact identity in proof 5.1, with c_F absolute and y_N boundary-plus-end-relative; the compact-replacement item proves the same finite convolution in proof 5.1. Its proof 6.1 establishes invariance of each local oriented intersection degree under an oriented homeomorphism, the finite-chain naturality actually used here. The collar isotopy fixes punctures, the filled tine, closing neighborhoods and the compact replacement support. Its lifted isotopy commutes with deck maps and fixes c_F because its point tracks are constant. Applying that local naturality, not an unsupported braid action for a boundary-moving map, gives the displayed scaled identity up to the permitted deck unit. The Laurent domain cancels the nonzero unit and Delta_F; the original detection lemma then applies to h1-inverse(M). Conjugation fixes every boundary point and puncture and leaves the tine unchanged, proving both implications. Thus the supplier proofs already establish the allegedly missing extensions.
